title: QL-1.02 Mutation gate: the changed lines are broken on purpose and the tests must catch every mutant
request: Closes quality-loop principle 2 (a test that survives a mutation is a weak test). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-0.03. Quality-loop principle set of 30 October 2026 (owner's order: implement as a gate for all dev).

tasks.title: Mutation runner over the diff
requirements: scripts/gate/mutate.mjs takes --base <sha> and --test <cmd>, lists the lines added or changed between base and the working tree in src/**/*.mjs, and applies one mutation at a time from a fixed operator set: === and !==, < and >=, > and <=, && and ||, true and false, + and - on numeric operands, a return value replaced by undefined, a call statement removed

before any mutant it runs the test command twice on the unmutated tree; a failure or a differing pass count there is NOISE and the run stops with exit 2, never judging a mutant (the twin's ME-MT oracle was confounded without this control)
each mutant runs in a temporary copy of the workdir that is removed in a finally block; the original tree is byte-identical after the run (checked by hashing the scope files before and after)

--json prints {mutants, killed, survived, noise, survivors:[{file,line,operator}]}; exit 1 when any mutant survives; a line carrying the comment mutate-ignore with a reason is skipped and counted as ignored
the script has no dependencies and its first line carries a version: comment
a NOISE run and a run with zero mutants never report survived 0 as a result: --json carries status (ok, noise or no-mutants) and the survived value counts only when status is ok

criteria.statement: On a fixture whose test checks the changed comparison the mutant is killed; on a fixture whose test only checks that a function returns, the mutant survives and the run exits 1; a flaky fixture stops with NOISE before any mutant
The runner exists

On the flaky fixture, and on a fixture whose test fails on the unmutated tree, the run exits 2 and the --json output has no numeric survived (null or absent), so a metric survived == 0 evaluated on that output fails

The fixture's changed lines are `export const gt = (a, b) => a > b;`, `export const tag = (s) => s + '===';` and a sum loop `for (let i = 0; i < n; i = i + 1)`, with a weak test that only checks each function returns. The run must exit 1 with killed 0, and every mutant it judged must pass node --check. A mutant that does not parse is reported as invalid and the looping mutant as timeout, never as killed. The run finishes within a bounded time and leaves no child process running

On a fixture whose weak test also reads a git-ignored file (listed in .gitignore and present in the workdir) and runs git rev-parse HEAD, the run either exits 1 with the weak mutant in survivors (the copy is complete) or exits 2 NOISE (the null control ran in the same kind of copy). It never exits 0, and killed is 0

The fixture's --test command records $PWD and the sha256 of the changed src file to a log outside the fixture. The test asserts that no run sees a mutated src file at the original workdir path. It then starts a second run whose --test blocks on a marker, SIGKILLs it while a mutant's test is running, and asserts that every file in the fixture workdir hashes exactly as before, git status --porcelain is unchanged, and no gate temp directory is left inside the workdir

Fixture repo: a base commit; a later commit that changes src/a/one.mjs; an uncommitted edit to src/two.mjs that inserts three lines above the changed comparison; an untracked new src/new.mjs; and git mv src/old.mjs src/b/renamed.mjs with one edited line. All have weak tests. With --base <base sha> the run exits 1, its survivors' {file,line} pairs are exactly the expected new-side coordinates in all four files, and no mutant sits on an unchanged line

A fixture has one changed line per operator kind in requirement 1, in both directions: === and !==, < and >=, > and <=, && and ||, true and false, numeric + and -, return x, and a bare call statement. It also has one line `return a > b && c;`. With a weak test that only checks each function returns, the survivors' operator set covers every kind and the two-site line yields two survivors. With a strong test on the same lines, every mutant is killed and the run exits 0
Two gate processes started together on the same weak-fixture checkout both exit 1 with identical survivors and killed 0, and the checkout hashes exactly as before

On a weak-test fixture, a changed line with a bare `// mutate-ignore` (no reason) and a changed line containing 'mutate-ignore' inside a string literal are still mutated and survive. A line with `// mutate-ignore: <reason>` is skipped. --json reports ignored as a count plus entries of {file,line,reason}
The run judged at least one mutant on the changed lines
Changes stay in scope

tasks.title: Every code contract carries the mutation criterion
requirements: the attest lint used by memev contract new warns when an implement task whose scope includes src/** has no metric criterion on scripts/gate/mutate.mjs with key survived, op ==, value 0
docs/CONTRACTS.md shows the criterion to copy and states that a test that survives a mutation is a weak test
the warning lives in the vendored attest lint (vendor/attest/contract.mjs), so memev contract new and contract decompose share it

criteria.statement: A draft with an implement task touching src and no mutation criterion gets the warning; one with it gets none
The contracts page carries the criterion and the weak-test rule
The full suite passes

A draft whose src-touching implement task carries only the metric survived == 0 still gets the warning. The warning clears only when the task also carries a metric on the same mutate.mjs command with key mutants, op >, value 0, and docs/CONTRACTS.md shows both criteria

Using newVault (test/helpers/tmp.mjs): a signed contract whose task carries a mandatory metric (a node -e cmd printing the JSON object survived:1, key survived, op ==, value 0) verifies FAIL. The same contract with survived:0 verifies PASS. A cmd that prints no JSON, or exits non-zero, verifies FAIL. A draft whose mutation metric is mandatory:false still gets the lint warning. This is red at base because contracts.mjs:235 returns BLOCKED

Through newVault: v.contractDraft with an implement task scoped ['src/**'] and no mutation metric returns a warnings entry naming the mutation criterion. So do v.contractFromRequest and v.contractAmend for the same task. The same draft carrying the canonical criterion returns no such warning

Each of these drafts gets the warning: a cmd that does not start with `node scripts/gate/mutate.mjs`; a --test that is not the workdir's project test command (projectTestCommand, contracts.mjs:80); --base HEAD; op, value or key other than survived == 0; mandatory:false; scope ['src/engine/x.mjs'], ['**'] or omitted; phase omitted. No warning appears for scope ['docs/**'], for a non-implement phase, or for the criterion parsed out of the fenced block in docs/CONTRACTS.md
Changes stay in scope
